title: Linearization of a functor with a projection formula
statement:
Let $\pi$ be a projection formula for $P\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ relative to a strong
monoidal $S\colon\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ ([def-sfb-projection-formula]). Let
$\mathcal B$ be a monoid object of $\mathcal D$, so $S\mathcal B$ is a monoid object of
$\mathcal C$. For an $S\mathcal B$-module object $M$ ([sk-def-sfb-module-objects]), the
morphism
$$
\mathcal B\otimes PM\xrightarrow{\pi^{-1}_{\mathcal B,M}}P(S\mathcal B\otimes M)
\xrightarrow{P\gamma_M}PM
$$
makes $PM$ a $\mathcal B$-module object, and $Pf$ is $\mathcal B$-linear for every
$S\mathcal B$-linear $f$. This defines the *linearization*
$$
P_{\mathcal B}\colon\Mod_{S\mathcal B}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal D),
$$
which commutes with the forgetful functors.

proof.text:
Write $B=\mathcal B$, $R=SB$, and let $\mu_B,\eta_B$ be the multiplication and unit of $B$. Apply [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport], clause 1, to the strong monoidal functor $S\colon\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$. Its lax structure maps are $\delta^{-1}$ and $\epsilon^{-1}$ in the notation of [def-sfb-projection-formula]. Thus $R$ is a monoid object with
$$\mu_R=S(\mu_B)\circ\delta_{B,B}^{-1},\qquad \eta_R=S(\eta_B)\circ\epsilon^{-1}.$$
For an $R$-module $M$, denote its given action by $\gamma_M$. Put $\phi_{L,M}=\pi_{L,M}^{-1}$ and define the proposed action $a_M=P(\gamma_M)\circ\phi_{B,M}\colon B\otimes PM\to PM$. These formulas specify the data without any choice.

source.place: displayed action; monoid structure supplied by det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport, clause 1

proof.text:
We will use inverse naturality of [def-sfb-projection-formula]. For $u\colon L\to L'$ and $v\colon M\to M'$ it gives
$$\phi_{L',M}\circ(u\otimes\mathrm{id}_{PM})=P(Su\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)\circ\phi_{L,M},$$
$$\phi_{L,M'}\circ(\mathrm{id}_L\otimes Pv)=P(\mathrm{id}_{SL}\otimes v)\circ\phi_{L,M}.$$
Indeed, the forward naturality equality is $\pi'\circ P(t)=t'\circ\pi$; composing on the left by $(\pi')^{-1}$ and on the right by $\pi^{-1}$ gives $P(t)\circ\pi^{-1}=(\pi')^{-1}\circ t'$. This proves both displayed equalities by cancellation of inverse isomorphisms.

source.place: naturality in L and M, inverted by cancellation

proof.text:
For the unit, use the module unit axiom in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and the formula $\eta_R=S\eta_B\circ\epsilon^{-1}$ from step 1. Precomposing $\gamma_M\circ(\eta_R\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)=\lambda_M$ with $\epsilon\otimes\mathrm{id}_M$ yields
$$\gamma_M\circ(S\eta_B\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)=\lambda_M\circ(\epsilon\otimes\mathrm{id}_M).$$
Inverse naturality at $u=\eta_B$ (step 2) and the unit compatibility in [def-sfb-projection-formula] now give
$$\begin{aligned}
a_M\circ(\eta_B\otimes\mathrm{id}_{PM})
&=P\bigl(\gamma_M\circ(S\eta_B\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)\bigr)\circ\phi_{\mathbf1,M}\\
&=P\bigl(\lambda_M\circ(\epsilon\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)\bigr)\circ\phi_{\mathbf1,M}
=\lambda_{PM}\circ\pi_{\mathbf1,M}\circ\phi_{\mathbf1,M}=\lambda_{PM}.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus $a_M$ is unital; only functoriality and inverse cancellation were used in the equalities.

source.place: unit compatibility, applied to the module unit axiom

proof.text:
For associativity set
$$c_M=\alpha_{R,R,M}\circ(\delta_{B,B}\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)\colon S(B\otimes B)\otimes M\to R\otimes(R\otimes M).$$
The module associativity axiom in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], precomposed with $\delta_{B,B}\otimes\mathrm{id}_M$, and $\mu_R\circ\delta_{B,B}=S\mu_B$ from step 1 give
$$\gamma_M\circ(S\mu_B\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)=\gamma_M\circ(\mathrm{id}_R\otimes\gamma_M)\circ c_M.\tag{A}$$
The associativity compatibility in [def-sfb-projection-formula] is
$$\alpha_{B,B,PM}\circ\pi_{B\otimes B,M}=(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes\pi_{B,M})\circ\pi_{B,R\otimes M}\circ P(c_M).$$
Compose this equality on the left with $\phi_{B,R\otimes M}\circ(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes\phi_{B,M})$ and on the right with $\phi_{B\otimes B,M}$. Cancellation, using that tensoring is a functor, gives
$$P(c_M)\circ\phi_{B\otimes B,M}=\phi_{B,R\otimes M}\circ(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes\phi_{B,M})\circ\alpha_{B,B,PM}.\tag{B}$$
Both (A) and (B) are direct substitutions in the cited axioms.

Apply inverse naturality at $u=\mu_B$ from step 2, then (A), then (B) from step 4, and finally inverse naturality in $M$ at $v=\gamma_M\colon R\otimes M\to M$:
$$\begin{aligned}
a_M\circ(\mu_B\otimes\mathrm{id}_{PM})
&=P\bigl(\gamma_M\circ(S\mu_B\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)\bigr)\circ\phi_{B\otimes B,M}\\
&=P\gamma_M\circ P(\mathrm{id}_R\otimes\gamma_M)\circ P(c_M)\circ\phi_{B\otimes B,M}\\
&=P\gamma_M\circ P(\mathrm{id}_R\otimes\gamma_M)\circ\phi_{B,R\otimes M}\circ(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes\phi_{B,M})\circ\alpha_{B,B,PM}\\
&=P\gamma_M\circ\phi_{B,M}\circ(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes P\gamma_M)\circ(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes\phi_{B,M})\circ\alpha_{B,B,PM}\\
&=a_M\circ(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes a_M)\circ\alpha_{B,B,PM}.
\end{aligned}$$
The naturality used here is precisely that of [def-sfb-projection-formula]; the penultimate-to-last equality is functoriality of $B\otimes-$. The equality is the action associativity axiom of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Together with step 3, it makes $(PM,a_M)$ a $B$-module. No strictness or symmetry of the monoidal categories is assumed.

source.place: the assertion that the displayed action makes PM a module; explicit associativity calculation

proof.text:
Let $f\colon M\to N$ be an $R$-linear map. The morphism condition of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] is $f\circ\gamma_M=\gamma_N\circ(\mathrm{id}_R\otimes f)$. Apply $P$ and use inverse naturality from [def-sfb-projection-formula] (step 2) at $v=f$ to obtain
$$\begin{aligned}
Pf\circ a_M
&=P(f\circ\gamma_M)\circ\phi_{B,M}\\
&=P\gamma_N\circ P(\mathrm{id}_R\otimes f)\circ\phi_{B,M}
=P\gamma_N\circ\phi_{B,N}\circ(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes Pf)
=a_N\circ(\mathrm{id}_B\otimes Pf).
\end{aligned}$$
This is exactly $B$-linearity of $Pf$.

source.place: the assertion that Pf is B-linear

proof.text: Define $P_B$ on objects by $(M,\gamma_M)\mapsto(PM,a_M)$ and on morphisms by $f\mapsto Pf$, as justified in steps 3, 5 and 6. By [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], identities and composition of module morphisms are the underlying ones in their monoidal category. Hence $P_B(\mathrm{id}_M)=P(\mathrm{id}_M)=\mathrm{id}_{PM}$ and $P_B(g\circ f)=P(g\circ f)=Pg\circ Pf$. Equal underlying morphisms are equal module morphisms because their linearity conditions are properties. If $U_R,U_B$ are the forgetful functors, then both $U_B\circ P_B$ and $P\circ U_R$ send $M$ to $PM$ and $f$ to $Pf$. Thus they agree, proving the claimed commutation with forgetful functors.

source.place: definition of P_B and commutation with the forgetful functors

proof_origin.place: displayed action and functor; explicit verification from def-sfb-projection-formula and sk-def-sfb-module-objects
